books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books.
stimulus.text: The Fugitive Slave Act was enforced in the North, and the North answered back. In February 1851 a crowd in Boston pulled Shadrach Minkins, a waiter seized as a runaway, out of a courtroom and sent him on to Canada. That September, near Christiana, Pennsylvania, Black residents and their neighbors fought off a Maryland slaveholder's party, and the slaveholder was killed. A month later, in Syracuse, New York, a crowd freed William “Jerry” Henry from the officers holding him. And in June 1854 federal troops marched Anthony Burns, a waiter seized in Boston, through the streets to a ship bound for Virginia.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The Burns case differed from the Minkins, Christiana, and Jerry episodes mainly in that

options.text: Burns was the only one seized in a Northern city.
options.misconception: Minkins was also seized in Boston, a Northern city; the difference is the outcome, not the place.

options.text: Burns escaped to Canada after his rescue.
options.misconception: Burns was returned to Virginia, not freed to Canada; Minkins was the one sent on to Canada.

options.text: Burns was seized by a slaveholder rather than by federal officers.
options.misconception: Burns was seized in Boston and held by officers; the passage credits federal troops with marching him to the ship.

options.text: federal troops enforced Burns's return, backing the law with force.

rationales.A: Minkins was also seized in Boston, a Northern city; the difference is the outcome, not the place.
rationales.B: Burns was returned to Virginia, not freed to Canada; Minkins was the one sent on to Canada.
rationales.C: Burns was seized in Boston and held by officers; the passage credits federal troops with marching him to the ship.
rationales.D: The passage says federal troops marched Burns “through the streets to a ship bound for Virginia” — the one case where federal force won.
rationales.general:
1. Hold the three rescues in mind: crowds won at Boston, Christiana, and Syracuse.
2. Turn to Burns: this time the crowd lost, and federal troops marched the prisoner through the streets.
3. Ask what the troops proved: that Washington would spend soldiers, not just paper, to enforce the law.
Remember: one case where the government wins can matter more than three where it loses — it shows what the government is willing to do.
